# Independent semantic review

## Decision

The frozen primary theorem and the main manuscript's modeled exclusion are equivalent. The package as a whole is **mismatch**, not approved: the supplement contains incorrect radius/parameter normalizations and several less serious declaration-strength or proof-attribution discrepancies. No critical error was found in the main argument. These findings concern the explanations, not a refutation of the Lean exclusion theorem.

## Coverage and provenance

I compared the frozen root, all 850 non-generated inventory declarations and their author statements/LaTeX explanations, and both configured generated families. The report has exactly one entry for each of those 850 declarations and one entry for each family. An independent inventory computation matched all 4,433 code-slice hashes and every indexed source-file hash, found all 850 exact author statements, explanations and source slices in LemmaSupplement.md, and found no duplicate author classification. The report's source_sha256 field is the inventory code_sha256, not the whole-file source hash. Generated review covered all 3,583 indexed declarations: 3,131 compact-family entries and 452 middle-face entries. The manuscripts' pre-existing status banner was not evidence for the mathematical decision.

The frozen lean-gate receipt reports success and only Classical.choice, Quot.sound and propext for the root; the dependency-audit receipt has exit code zero. I did not rerun the Lean build or treat compilation as semantic equivalence. Source comparison and the explicit model/objective bridges below are what establish the claimed meaning.

## Primary theorem and minimization semantics

FourArcCandidate has only h and alpha with 0<h<=1 and 0<alpha<pi/2. SatisfiesCMVTypeIVHypotheses adds exactly lambda>1 and lambda*cos(alpha)=h. Neither definition assumes minimality, stationarity, a certificate or a successful comparison. IsWeightedPerimeterMinimizer universally compares the candidate with every AdmissibleCompetitor of exactly the same weighted area, in the direction P(candidate)<=P(competitor). A strict real-valued reverse inequality disproves it.

The density is one on the CLOSED strip |y|<=1 and lambda outside. Weighted area is the Lebesgue density integral. Admissible perimeter is canonically the density integral over the complete topological frontier in the Euclidean L2 realization, transported back to coordinates. It is not an arbitrary boundary measure. The general competitor constructor requires measurable carrier and both density-integrability conditions. Its name FinitePerimeterRegion does not identify it with every BV/Caccioppoli set modulo null changes. The main manuscript states this distinction and does not import the CMV classification as a formal hypothesis or conclusion. Relative to the frozen MODELED claim, this is not a conditional scalar fragment or a theorem only about four-arc-to-four-arc comparisons.

The geometric proof identifies the actual four-arc and replacement frontiers, all component Hausdorff lengths, and finite junction nullity. It includes the replacement's exposed bottom chord at density one. The type-(iii) realization covers every 0<s<1, including its exterior major-cap branch s<1/2 and zero-length bottom segment s=1/2. Its scalar area and perimeter are proved equal to the actual integrals; hasModeledCompetitor explicitly builds a general admissible carrier. Four-arc objective identification includes h=1. Thus a scalar improvement is genuinely promoted to an admissible equal-area competitor, not merely to a formal inequality between unrelated functions.

## Analytic reduction and quantifiers

The manuscript B3 includes pi/2; LeanSuffixAnalytic.typeThreeAngle does not. The entries that explicitly explain this shift, the CMVSuffixModel bridge, and the objective formulas are consistent. K3 and K4 are the exact area derivative numerators, A_i'=K_i/h^3 and P_i'=K_i/h^2 on the open regular domain. The reciprocal-cube radical comparison is valid throughout -1<q<1, including q=0, so K3 monotonicity extends across s=1/2.

A StationaryEqualAreaPair contains regular curvatures, s>1/2, equal area and K4=0; negative K3 and strict P3<P4 are separate inputs. The negative-fold descending root is unique only in that branch; the argument does not assert uniqueness of every possible equal-area root. Divergence of A3 at zero and the global A4 fold minimum give a descending root for every 0<t<=1. The root-order proof derives r(t)<t from the same-curvature area inequality and negative-fold monotonicity. Compact trapping and uniqueness give continuity; nonvanishing A3prime then gives implicit differentiation. The resulting gap derivative is (r(t)-t)A4prime(t). Interior sign arguments and one-sided continuity at t=1 put the largest gap at the stationary fold. No derivative at the radical-singular endpoint t=1 is asserted.

The middle-face root map is (-F,C4,E,C3), in the xi,eta,rho,sigma coordinate order. The source root proof uses the special triangular structure: continuous incidence projections in eta and sigma, followed by one-dimensional intermediate value arguments in xi and rho. Strict low/high face signs and the full principal-angle branches justify a simultaneous exact root; small numerical residuals alone are not used. K3 and G are uniformly negative on the box and therefore negative at the selected root. Existence is for each density separately; no continuous selection of stationary pairs in density is required.

## Exact density coverage and high-density splice

The first prototype covers [51/50,102001/100000], all 113 middle bricks cover [102001/100000,25781/25000], and the right prototype covers [25781/25000,33/32]. Exact rational seam checks found adjacent endpoints equal, including the nonuniform final middle brick. The first two compact boxes are nongenerated and explicitly included. Generated compact boxes 2 through 1023 begin at 118329/114688 and end at 9/7; together with boxes zero and one they cover [33/32,9/7]. All local candidate-boundary statements/proofs and compact Conditions payloads have the same audited contract, with no stationary-candidate or extra-certificate input. Each of the six compact sign-leaf proof forms is identical across all 1,022 generated boxes, referring to exact local rational intervals and sound atom/centered enclosures. All 65 indexed compact batch/prefix endpoints agree with the corresponding unions, and batch proof references cover the indexed boxes rather than skipping a first interval.

The high-density branch uses the inverse of unit-CHORD segment area on the full (0,pi) angle range. The global saving minimum is attained at the positive xstar with value 3*cos(theta_star), and the exact rational 1.2581840884 gives strict g(X)>1/lambda. The division-free identity is P(replacement)-P(candidate)=c*(1-lambda*g(X)); under the positive primary density it is equivalent to the manuscript's opposite-signed saving formula. The final split includes the seams 33/32 and 9/7 and uses the exact positive gap 9/7-1.2581840884=481778453/17500000000. No conclusion below 51/50 or sharpness of that endpoint follows, and the manuscript does not assert either.

## Critical supplement errors

The source symbol unitCircleArc is misleadingly named but unambiguous: u_r(s)=r*exp(i*s/r). Its second argument is signed arclength, not angle. The supplement instead writes exp(it), gives real and imaginary coordinates cos(t),sin(t), and gives the unit-radius chord formula 2|sin((t-s)/2)|. The actual coordinate formulas are r*cos(s/r), r*sin(s/r), and the distance is 2r|sin((s-t)/(2r))| for r>0. Exact counterexamples are u_2(0)=2 rather than 1, Im u_2(pi)=2 rather than 0, and dist(u_2(0),u_2(2pi))=4 rather than 0. These errors are recorded at unitCircleArc, unitCircleArc_dist, unitCircleArc_re and unitCircleArc_im; the related radius-one descriptions lose the formal generality.

The same confusion affects the partition and length explanations. capPartitionPoint partitions [-r*theta,r*theta] in arclength coordinates. The polygonal limit and symmetric arc measure are 2r*theta, not angular span 2theta. The arbitrary-interval no-full-turn hypothesis is v-u<2*pi*r, not v-u<2*pi independently of r. A radius-1/2 curve on [0,3*pi/2] satisfies the latter incorrect bound but runs beyond a full turn: its image length is pi, not 3*pi/2. The formal hypothesis excludes it. The polygonal limit theorem is algebraic for arbitrary real r, and negative r cannot be described as a polygonal length. These are mathematical normalization/domain errors in the declaration guide, including entries classified main but printed in the supplement. MainProof.md itself retains the correct geometric radius factors, so the main-proof critical-error list is empty.

## Other exact-declaration discrepancies

The individual entries distinguish harmless formal generalizations from errors: unconditional slab perimeter estimates versus stationary specialization; interior derivative negativity versus a stronger closed-slab fold assumption; a continuous simple root versus a specifically descending root; absent measurable-set premises; the full [0,pi] domain of F monotonicity; type-(iii) closure endpoints in Rolle/root-order lemmas; and the unrestricted rational domains of Taylor soundness. theta_star_spec supplies only the root equation, with interval membership in a separate declaration; thetaOf_image supplies only one inclusion, with the reverse inclusion available from thetaOf_mem. thetaOf has an omitted nonpositive-input totalization to pi/2, unused by the positive-area proof. The cap-saving factorization with 1/lambda needs nonzero density even though the cited division-free identity does not. Finally asCompetitor is a projection of an existing realization; the general-constructor/integrability construction belongs to hasModeledCompetitor. These local scope/proof-attribution discrepancies do not create an unproved premise in the primary theorem.

## External citation verification

The sole authored external citation has an exact stable version locator, arXiv:0906.1256v1, and numbered internal locators. I checked the versioned arXiv record and the frozen PDF: strip density and Propositions 3.5-3.6 on printed p.13; Lemma 3.8 on p.15; Proposition 3.9 on p.18; Conjecture 3.12 and equations (26)-(27) on p.19; Theorem 3.16 beginning p.22 and continuing pp.23-24; the cap-replacement comparison and Remark 3.17 on p.24. Crossref independently confirms the journal citation: Journal of Geometric Analysis 20(2) (2010), 243-290, DOI 10.1007/s12220-009-9109-4. No citation-locator defect was found. The source article's finite-perimeter framework differs from the package's canonical-frontier model, and the manuscript explicitly leaves that source-to-model bridge outside the theorem.

## Independent diagnostics and conclusion

I ran source/inventory/hash checks, the all-index exact-rational family audit, and independent direct-formula diagnostics. Radius counterexamples reproduced the incompatible supplement values. Fifteen equal-area numerical diagnostics at lambda=51/50,33/32,9/7, including t=1 and roots below 1/2, all had r(t)<t, negative K3 and negative perimeter gap; for example at lambda=51/50 the stationary comparison gave t approximately 0.9829151230, s approximately 0.9568098166 and gap approximately -0.0081852273. These floating-point diagnostics are explicitly NOT a universal proof or a replacement for the exact interval argument; they are independent semantic checks. The zero bottom chord at s=1/2 was also exercised.

Conclusion: retain the modeled primary exclusion, but correct the supplement's radius/arclength statements and the enumerated exact-declaration discrepancies before claiming package-wide semantic equivalence. No Lean-source change is justified by this review, and no full-CMV classification or BV-perimeter equivalence is certified here.
